daily_brief: The day's headlines are dominated by escalating tensions between Washington and Kyiv, as Ukraine accused the US of disrupting Starlink satellite services critical to its drone operations, with Elon Musk suggesting the US government controls any restrictions [BBC, Globe and Mail, RFI]. President Zelensky announced Ukraine would resume strikes on Russian refineries after what he called a failed 'energy ceasefire' unilaterally declared by President Trump [Al Jazeera, Globe and Mail]. In Europe, EU leaders convene for contentious budget negotiations worth nearly two trillion euros, racing to reach agreement before France's presidential election amid fears of eurosceptic gains [France 24, RFI]. Asian markets suffered sharp losses, with the KOSPI falling over 7% and the Nikkei down 4%, triggered by higher-than-expected US inflation data and AI investment concerns [Nikkei Asia]. Tragic news from Pakistan where at least 17 children and a teacher were killed in a school roof collapse in Peshawar [The Hindu, Al Jazeera]. Meanwhile, China and North Korea opened a long-delayed border bridge, signaling deepening ties between the Cold War-era allies [Nikkei Asia, France 24, Al Jazeera].

top_stories.headline: Ukraine Reports Starlink Disruptions as Musk Points to US Government Control
bullets: Ukraine reported that Starshield, the military-grade SpaceX satellite system, imposed speed limits of 100mph on Tuesday night, disrupting drone attack missions and air defense operations
Elon Musk stated on X that Starshield systems are owned and controlled by the US government, with limits decided by the US military and ultimately the president
President Zelensky called the disruptions 'a big mistake' that 'will bring a lot of human losses' and appealed for service restoration
Partial connectivity was restored by Wednesday evening according to Ukraine's former defence minister Mykhailo Fedorov

sources.name: BBC World
sources.framing_note: Focused on Musk's statements and technical details of the restrictions

sources.name: RFI English
sources.framing_note: Emphasized European reliance on US technology and lack of homegrown alternatives

sources.name: Globe and Mail
sources.framing_note: Highlighted worsening US-Ukraine ties and Trump's pressure on Zelensky

sources.name: The Hindu
sources.framing_note: Framed as potential US desertion of Ukraine with detailed explainer format

top_stories.headline: Ukraine Resumes Strikes on Russian Refineries After Failed Energy Ceasefire
bullets: President Zelensky told the Financial Times that Ukraine was 'done' with the energy ceasefire and would resume attacks on Russian oil refineries
Russia reported a Ukrainian drone strike on an oil refinery in Ryazan, about 180km south of Moscow, causing a fire
Trump had unilaterally announced an energy ceasefire on Sunday, but Russia continued striking Ukrainian energy infrastructure, leaving 600,000 Ukrainians without power
Zelensky criticized Trump's 'favouritism toward Russia' and expressed frustration at alleged withdrawal of US intelligence sharing

sources.name: Al Jazeera
sources.framing_note: Emphasized that Trump's ceasefire was unilateral and not publicly confirmed by other parties

sources.name: Globe and Mail
sources.framing_note: Detailed Zelensky's anger at 'dangerous' withdrawal of US intelligence

sources.name: Le Monde
sources.framing_note: Article focused on Washington limiting support amid Russian attacks

top_stories.headline: EU Leaders Face High-Stakes Budget Showdown Ahead of French Election
bullets: EU leaders meet Thursday to negotiate the bloc's next long-term budget covering 2028-2034, worth nearly two trillion euros
Leaders are racing to reach agreement by December, fearing eurosceptic wins in upcoming elections, particularly France's presidential vote
Marine Le Pen, frontrunner in the French election, called it a 'democratic scandal' to adopt a budget before next year's votes and wants to slash France's EU contribution
Key disputes include funding levels for agriculture, defense, economic competitiveness versus US and China, and migration return hubs in Africa

sources.name: France 24
sources.framing_note: Video coverage emphasizing clash over budget and Ukraine support

sources.name: RFI English
sources.framing_note: Detailed analysis of political pressures and Le Pen's opposition

top_stories.headline: Asian Markets Plunge on US Inflation Data and AI Investment Concerns
bullets: South Korea's KOSPI fell more than 7% and Japan's Nikkei dropped 4% on Thursday morning
The sell-off followed higher-than-expected US consumer price index data showing inflation accelerated in September
Markets were also affected by concerns about artificial intelligence investment levels and debt
Japanese Finance Minister said the G20 discussed concerns over yields and currency volatility at the Bangkok meeting

sources.name: Nikkei Asia
sources.framing_note: Provided detailed regional market data and linked to G20 finance ministers meeting

top_stories.headline: At Least 17 Children Killed in Pakistan School Roof Collapse
bullets: The roof of a private school collapsed in Dir Colony, inner-city Peshawar, on Thursday morning
At least 17 students and one teacher were killed, with all deceased children aged 13 or younger
More than 40 people were injured and rescue teams continued searching debris for those still trapped
Police arrested the school owner, with authorities accusing those responsible of severe negligence

sources.name: The Hindu
sources.framing_note: Straightforward news coverage with official statements from police and hospital

sources.name: Al Jazeera
sources.framing_note: Higher casualty figure of 29, included detail about owner's arrest and negligence accusations
